diagrams.title: From Need to Vendor Monitoring
diagrams.subtitle: Selection → agreement → monitoring: each step produces an auditable artifact.

quiz.question: At which step does the right-to-audit clause apply?

nodes.label: Scoped need
nodes.detail: Define what is outsourced to the third party, the data involved, jurisdiction, and internal constraints before any solicitation.
nodes.exam: An unclear need makes due diligence impossible: it is the starting point of the entire process.

nodes.label: Selection
nodes.detail: Gauge interest (EOI), gather information (RFI), request a proposal (RFP), then a price quote (RFQ). Due diligence verifies security and compliance.
nodes.exam: RFP = proposal, RFQ = quote. These documents are not in the provided books.

nodes.label: Agreement
nodes.detail: The MSA sets general terms, the SOW defines the engagement, the SLA sets service levels, the NDA covers confidentiality, and MOU/MOA defines the level of commitment.
nodes.exam: Rules of Engagement (ROE) bound any penetration test conducted by or for the vendor.

nodes.label: Monitoring
nodes.detail: SLA tracking, periodic evaluation, compliance attestation, and right to audit. The third-party register centralizes responsibilities.
nodes.exam: Right to audit and the third-party register are §5.3 concepts absent from the books.

nodes.label: Limits & exit
nodes.detail: Document headcount, resources, environment, jurisdiction, ROI, insurance, and vendor lock-in. Plan exit clauses and exportable formats.
nodes.exam: An abrupt exit without a migration plan is riskier than monitored contractual drift.
